title: Tuga A8 vs Tuga A10: 8 Inch or 10 Inch Rugged Android Tablet?
description: Tuga A8 (£379) or Tuga A10 (£449)? £70 apart and both 680g. The A8 is brighter with the bigger battery; the A10 has the 10.1 inch Full HD screen for drawings.
summary: Both 680g and £70 apart: the A8 is brighter at 800 nits with a 10000mAh battery and glove mode, the A10 has the 10.1 inch 1920 x 1200 screen for drawings and spreadsheets but is dimmer at 350 nits.
lede: For sole traders and small firms choosing between the two Android tablets in the range. The short answer: the A8 at £379 for outdoor and one-handed work, the A10 at £449 for drawings, plans and spreadsheets.
verdict: Buy the Tuga A10 at £449 if you read drawings and plans on it; buy the Tuga A8 at £379 if it works outdoors or in one hand. The gap is £70. Both run Android 14 with 8GB of RAM and 128GB of storage, are sealed to IP68, tested to MIL-STD-810H, and weigh 680g. The £70 buys a bigger, sharper screen: 10.1 inches at 1920 x 1200 against 8 inches at 1280 x 800. The trade-off is brightness and battery: 350 nits against 800 on the A8, and 8000mAh against 10000mAh.

Pay the £70 if you read drawings, plans or spreadsheets on the tablet. On an 8 inch screen a large drawing needs more panning and zooming than on 10.1 inches. The A10 also has dual SIM 4G for sites where one network is patchy, and it is the only one of the two with the paid 3-Year Warranty option, at £65. It is the tablet for a site cabin or a desk dock. Brightness matters less there. In direct sun on an open site, a roof or a dashboard mount, the A10 is harder to read than the A8. The construction page goes through where it earns its place for drawings.

Keep the £70 if the tablet lives outdoors or in one hand. The A8 has glove mode, which the A10 does not list, and a 10000mAh battery a quarter larger than the A10's 8000mAh. Both weigh 680g, so the difference in the hand is size: the A10 measures 250 x 167mm, and only the A8 is listed as fitting a van door pocket and one hand up a ladder. For forms, photos, route maps and quotes, the A8 is the cheaper choice, and the field service page covers where the A8 fits against the A6 and W8. If one job decides it, tell us what you do and we will say which we would buy.
chooseA: You read the screen in direct sun on roofs, open sites or a van dashboard: 800 nits against the A10's 350.
You hold it in one hand up a ladder or drop it in a van door pocket: the A8 is listed as fitting both, at the same 680g as the A10.
You want the larger battery: 10000mAh against the A10's 8000mAh, with 18W fast charging listed.
You work in gloves through winter: the A8 lists glove mode and the A10 does not.
You want a USB-A port as well as USB-C: the A8 lists both, the A10 lists USB-C.
chooseB: You read drawings, PDF plans or full spreadsheets on the tablet, and check your own viewer apps run: 10.1 inches at 1920 x 1200 against 8 inches at 1280 x 800.
The tablet lives in a site cabin or on a desk dock, out of direct sun, where brightness matters less.
You work where one network is patchy: the A10 has dual SIM 4G, the A8 lists 4G LTE.
You want cover beyond the included 12 months: the A10 is the only one of the two with the paid 3-Year Warranty option, at £65.
You store a lot of photos, plans or offline maps on the device: microSD up to 2TB against 512GB on the A8.

faq.q: Is the Tuga A10 worth £70 more than the Tuga A8?
faq.a: For drawings and plans, yes; for forms, photos and route maps, the A8 does the job for £70 less. The A10 costs £449 and the A8 £379. The £70 buys a 10.1 inch 1920 x 1200 screen in place of 8 inches at 1280 x 800, dual SIM 4G, a microSD slot rated to 2TB, and the option of the paid 3-Year Warranty at £65. It gives up brightness (350 nits against 800), battery (8000mAh against 10000mAh), glove mode and the USB-A port, neither of which the A10 lists. If you spend the day in PDF plans, BIM viewers or spreadsheets, pay it and buy the Tuga A10. If you fill in forms, take photos and follow routes, buy the Tuga A8 and keep the £70. Buying several? Device discounts run from 3 percent at two to 10 percent at ten or more, see bulk orders.

faq.q: Can I read the Tuga A10 screen outdoors?
faq.a: It is 350 nits and not listed as sunlight readable, so direct sun is harder work than on the A8, which is 800 nits and listed as sunlight readable. Indoors or in a site cabin it is the better screen for plans: sharper at 1920 x 1200 against the A8's 1280 x 800, and bigger at 10.1 inches against 8. If most of your day is on open sites or roofs, choose the A8, or keep the A10 for the cabin and the desk dock. The construction page says the same thing with the trades spelled out.

faq.q: Which lasts longer on a charge, the A8 or the A10?
faq.a: We cannot say. The A8 has the larger battery, 10000mAh against the A10's 8000mAh, but neither lists a run time in hours and the two have different screens and processors, so we will not guess. The A8 lists 18W fast charging; the A10 lists quick charge without a figure. Both take the 12V DC Car Charger (£26), the Vehicle Mounting Dock (£109) has a DC power input, and the Charging Dock (£49.99) is listed for the A10 only, all on the accessories page. Both are rated to work from -20°C to 60°C. Our guide to rugged tablets in winter covers what the cold does to either battery and why the A8's glove mode matters in January.

faq.q: Are the A8 and A10 the same size and weight?
faq.a: Same weight, different size. Both weigh 680g, so the A10 is not the heavier tablet, it is the bigger one: 250 x 167mm and 14.5mm thick. The A8 does not list dimensions, but with an 8 inch screen against 10.1, only the A8 is listed as fitting a van door pocket and one hand; if you need a figure for a case or a mount, ask us. The same Vehicle Mounting Dock and Rugged Carry Case (fits tablets up to 10.1 inches) are listed for both; the Charging Dock is listed for the A10 only.
